findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` method definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
findings.body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined: one at line 145 accepting `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and another at line 149 accepting `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first. Any existing callers that pass width and height as separate numeric arguments (e.g., `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 200)`) will now have `200` interpreted as the `opts` hash, causing silent misbehavior or errors. The first method is dead code.

findings.title: Tempfile position not reset after external process rewrites the file
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` invokes a shell command (`convert`) that truncates and rewrites the file at `tempfile.path`. The Ruby `Tempfile` object's file descriptor position is not updated by this external write and may remain at or beyond the old EOF. When `Upload.create_for` subsequently reads from `tempfile`, it may read zero bytes or partial/corrupt data. A `tempfile.rewind` (or `tempfile.seek(0)`) is needed after the downsize loop before passing the tempfile to `Upload.create_for`.

findings.title: Client-side upload size limit hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring admin-configured site settings
findings.body: The previous code read the limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, respecting the administrator's configuration. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB. This means users can upload files up to 10 MB regardless of the configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`. For attachments (non-images), there is no server-side downsize logic, so oversized attachments will be accepted. The error message shown to users will also incorrectly state 10 MB as the limit.

findings.title: Downsize loop does not check return value; may loop uselessly on failure
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when the underlying `convert` command fails (e.g., corrupt or unsupported image). The while-loop ignores this return value, so if downsize fails on the first attempt it will retry 4 more times with no effect, wasting time and potentially holding the request open. The loop should break early when `downsize` returns `false`.

findings.title: Image still uploaded even if it exceeds max_image_size_kb after all downsize attempts
findings.body: After up to 5 downsize iterations, there is no final check that `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. If the image is still too large (e.g., a very large PNG that doesn't shrink much with dimension reduction), it is uploaded and stored without any error returned to the user, defeating the purpose of the size limit.

findings.title: API URL download limit raised to 10 MB without corresponding server-side guard for non-images
findings.body: The download limit for API-provided URLs was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. For non-image uploads via the API (attachments), there is no downsize logic and no subsequent size check, so an API caller can store attachments up to 10 MB regardless of the configured `max_attachment_size_kb`.
